From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 13:22:00 -0800
Subject: RI playbook draft for marketplace operator vs processor — draft attached

Hannah / all —

Attached is v1 of a customer-facing playbook. High-level bullets included below for quick review. I kept it non-legal but accurate for procurement:

- Position: Redwood acts as a service provider (processor) for customer-owned content and metadata when the customer (MerchCo) controls seller onboarding and determines uses. In marketplace flows where Redwood processes seller PII on behalf of MerchCo and does not independently monetize that data, we qualify as a service provider under CCPA/CPRA.

- Resale/sale: We do not use customer data for our own purposes or sell it. For marketplace features that expose seller listings to buyers, that publication is an action requested by MerchCo — not a resale by Redwood. If MerchCo later uses data to build a separate buyer-targeting product beyond the platform scope, that would be a customer action and not Redwood's resale.

- Deletion & erasure: We support deletion APIs and account-level erase commands. Our SLO: 30 days for full KV purge from hot storage and 180 days for long-tail backups (exceptions for legal hold). We can implement a staggered purge for seller vs buyer metadata.

- Telemetry: Aggregated telemetry (latency, feature usage) is retained for 24 months. Any telemetry that contains direct identifiers is treated as PD and handled per the DPA; we redact or pseudonymize KVs used for caching and analytics where feasible.

- Onshore fallback & subprocessors: We provide an onshore fallback option (US-only routing) for telemetry and request routing. Subprocessors are documented in our subprocessor list; we will provide a residency attestation for critical subprocessors.

Next steps: Karthik / Jonas — please review infra bullets and add a short paragraph about logs, KV cache retention, and exception handling for subpoenas. I'll iterate and produce a single-page memo to send to MerchCo.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: RI-operator-vs-processor-playbook-v1.docx)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RI playbook draft for marketplace operator vs processor — infra notes

Marissa — good draft. A few infra clarifications to make the memo actionable for MerchCo procurement:

- KV cache: cache keys are TTL'ed per route. Deleting a record invalidates the KV immediately; however the underlying shard may hold an encrypted copy until compaction. Recommend we state 'KV invalidation immediate; full physical removal within 30 days for active shards, 180 days for backups'.

- Logs & request traces: request-level traces persist 90 days by default (configurable). We can provide a scoped export for specific customer queries as evidence.

- Subprocessors: list critical subprocessors and indicate 'onshore fallback' capability for each. If MerchCo requires contractual onshore-only subprocessors we should flag potential limitations and pricing impact.

- Subpoena/legal hold: we can assert that Redwood will notify MerchCo and preserve the minimal data required to comply; this may pause deletion timelines for affected records.

I'll add two short sentences to the infra appendix and send back.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Serving Infrastructure — Redwood Inference
